# Copilot instructions for Caerus

Caerus is a GTK4/Rust package manager GUI for Void Linux, built directly
on `libxbps`. Three-crate Cargo workspace:

- `xbps-sys/` — raw FFI bindings to `libxbps`, generated by `bindgen` via
  `pkg-config` (`libxbps.pc`).
- `caerus/` — the GTK4 app. Runs fully unprivileged, never touches root.
  `src/backend/` is toolkit-agnostic; `src/ui/` is hand-built GTK4 widget
  code (no `.ui`/GtkBuilder templates).
- `caerus-helper/` — the one privileged component, spawned via `pkexec`,
  deliberately zero external dependencies. Parses a small line protocol
  over stdin/stdout (`INSTALL`/`REMOVE`/`PURGE`/`SYNC`/`HOLD`/`VKPURGE`/
  repo toggles/…) and shells out to the matching `xbps-*` CLI tool.

## Hard invariants — do not violate these

- **Exactly one OS thread ever touches the `xbps_handle`** (see the
  worker-thread setup in `caerus/src/backend/package_store.rs`).
  `libxbps` does not tolerate concurrent/re-entrant `xbps_init`/`xbps_end`
  calls — this was the root cause of a real crash in an earlier version.
  Never add a code path where a second thread calls into `libxbps`
  directly; route everything through the existing worker + `mpsc::Sender`
  pattern.
- **Every subprocess call uses an argv array, never shell
  interpolation.** `caerus-helper` rejects control characters in
  user-supplied strings (repo URLs, alternative group/pkg names, kernel
  versions) independently of whatever the GUI already validated — the
  privileged side never trusts the unprivileged side.
- **`ADDREPO`/`REMOVEREPO`/`ENABLEREPO`/`DISABLEREPO` only ever touch
  exact `repository=<url>` lines** in `/etc/xbps.d/*.conf`. Vendor repos
  under `/usr/share/xbps.d` are never edited in place — disabling one
  writes a same-name override into `/etc/xbps.d` instead (the xbps.d(5)
  shadowing rule).

## A GTK reentrancy bug class worth knowing before touching dialogs

A modal confirmation dialog (e.g. `remove_confirm.rs`, `deps_confirm.rs`)
whose button handler both (a) destroys the dialog and (b) mutates the
package list's backing `GListStore` (via `PackageStore::set_mark`, which
splices — rebinding whichever `ColumnView` row holds the affected
package) **will segfault deep in GTK** if the store mutation runs
synchronously, because the handler can be invoked while a *different*
top-level window's own signal-emission stack (e.g. the checkbox that
opened this dialog) is still unwinding. Fixed instances of this pattern:
call `dlg.destroy()` first, then defer the store mutation + callback via
`glib::source::idle_add_local_once`. Apply the same fix to any new
dialog with this shape rather than the more common `cb(true);
dlg.destroy();` ordering used elsewhere in the codebase (which is only
safe when the callback doesn't touch the package-list store directly).

## Conventions

- **No explanatory code comments.** Well-named identifiers and short
  functions carry the explanation. Put rationale in the commit message,
  not the diff.
- **Commit messages are one line.** No long bodies/bullet lists in the
  commit description.
- Duplicated logic gets a shared helper rather than repeated inline
  blocks — e.g. `package_store::package_obj_at(list, i)` is the one
  place that downcasts a `GListStore` item to `PackageObject` and logs
  on mismatch; don't reintroduce inline `match obj.downcast::<...>()`
  blocks for that.
- Every async worker query goes through `PackageStore::request()` +
  a `*_async(name, callback)` wrapper with a stale-reply guard comparing
  the currently-selected package — never `rx.recv()` on the main thread.

## Before opening a PR

Run the full local-CI-equivalent matrix, both feature configs:

```
cargo build --workspace && cargo build --workspace --features caerus/adwaita
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features caerus/adwaita -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

**Check `git log --oneline -20` on `main` before starting work that looks
like it might already be in flight.** This repo has had more than one
agent branch reimplement the same fix independently because it branched
from a commit that predated another PR merging the equivalent change —
wasted effort and a needless merge conflict both times. If your intended
fix touches `package_store.rs`'s `PackageObject` downcasting or
`caerus-helper`'s `run_xbps`/`respond_ok_or` error handling, it has
likely already been addressed — check history first.
